newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says help in Zaire can only follow ceasefire.
newsitem.headline: EU says help in Zaire can only follow ceasefire.

text.p: The European Union said on Sunday a ceasefire must be declared in eastern Zaire before more than a million refugees caught in the raging cross-border conflict and facing potential catastrophe could be helped on a mass scale.
"The essential first requirement is a ceasefire...Only then can we begin the massive humanitarian job that needs to be done," a statement from the EU's Irish presidency said.
"Only then too can we begin addressing the long-standing wider problem of the over one million Rwandan refugees in that area and in the region as a whole," it added.

The statement, received in Brussels, was issued on behalf of Irish Foreign Affairs Minister Dick Spring and Ireland's Minister of State for Development Cooperation Joan Burton. Ireland holds the rotating EU presidency.

A two-week lightning offensive in eastern Zaire by Tutsi rebels, some backed by government forces from neighbouring Rwanda, has thrown Zaire's army into disarray and left the mostly Hutu refugees cut off and at high risk.
The EU said it was "intensely involved" in efforts to bring about a ceasefire, through its special envoy to the region Aldo Ajello and other contacts being made to support his work.

Spring and Burton had been in contact with other EU colleagues, the United Nations, the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees, and African leaders in the Great Lakes region about ways to end the conflict.
Leaders from seven regional states including Rwanda are expected to attend a summit in Nairobi on Tuesday on the crisis.
But Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo has said that while Rwandan troops are fighting in Zaire there can be no peace talks. Rwanda denies it troops have crossed the border to help Tutsi rebels.
On Thursday European Union ministers are due to meet in Brussels at the request of Belgium, a former colonial power of the central African country.
Ireland's Burton, who is to chair the meeting, said its priority was to ensure a humanitarian disaster was averted.
In a separate statement the European Commissioner for Humanitarian aid, Emma Bonino, joined calls for supply routes to be opened to let emergency aid through to the refugees.

"800,000 people, more than half children under 15, have sat down to die in an area between the shores of Lake Kivu and the refugee camp of Mugunga, north of Goma, without food, clean water and medical assistance," she said.
She appealed to the Rwandan government to guarantee safe routes to the Mugunga camp with passage through Kivu Lake and Goma airport, and also to take its share of responsibility for the refugees.
